:rotating_light: _new alert — needs human_
Channel: `alert-frontend-errors`  -  confidence: 0.78  -  bug-type guess: env

*This is 1 of 10 related alerts fired by the same monitor during a single 38-min incident.*

Symptoms:
• Monitor 77419271 ("Unusual number of XHR errors for account") fired 10 times between 14:27–15:05 EDT today
• All errors: `"Failed to load"` (HTTP status 0, network-level failure) on `GET /gateway/syncutil/syncwidget/<account>/GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync`
• 18+ distinct customer accounts affected simultaneously in the first 10 minutes alone
• Error origin: `network` — clients could not reach the syncutil backend endpoint at all
Trace IDs: n/a — `status_code: 0` errors don't produce server-side traces (client-side network failures only)

Likely cause: Transient backend outage of the *syncutil gateway* service (~38 min duration). The simultaneous impact across many unrelated accounts rules out per-account data issues; the "Failed to load" / HTTP 0 pattern rules out application-level errors in `method-ui`.

Additional context:
• Current frontend version `master.2026-04-24_14:32:32z` — deployed 7 days ago, no recent change
• Monitor is now *OK* (auto-resolved at 15:05:12 EDT) — no active incident
• No Datadog monitors exist for the `syncutil` service specifically → no direct health visibility
Suggested next action: *Monitor* — incident has self-resolved. Consider adding a Datadog monitor on the `syncutil` service itself so future outages are caught before XHR errors accumulate to threshold.

:rotating_light: _new alert — needs human_
Channel: `alert-system`  -  confidence: 0.55  -  bug-type guess: `env`

*Symptoms:*
• RabbitMQ queue depth spiked from baseline ~127 → peak *2,740 messages* starting ~15:18 EDT, was at ~988 at alert time (15:57 EDT)
• Queue was draining steadily; a *second spike started ~16:18 EDT* (currently ~1,966 messages)
• No backend service errors in Datadog (empty results across all prod services last 75 min)
• No Redis errors
• No recent deploys correlated with spike start
*Trace IDs:* none available (infra-level alert, no traces)

*24h baseline comparison:*
• Yesterday same window: avg=1,024 msgs, max=2,672 msgs
• Today's peak 2,740 is only slightly above yesterday's max — pattern may be *normal cyclic batch processing*
*Likely cause:* Recurring RabbitMQ queue depth spike from periodic batch job publishing. The cyclic drain-and-refill pattern is consistent with yesterday.

*Suggested next action:* Monitor queue drain. If this pattern repeats at same cadence daily, consider adding a `false-alarm` KB entry to silence it for 4h windows.

_Note: ES logs unavailable (403 allowlist block). Alert message body not visible (Slack attachments not surfaced by MCP)._

:rotating_light: _new alert — needs human_
Channel: `alert-system`  -  confidence: 0.60  -  bug-type guess: `env`

*Symptoms:*
• Second RabbitMQ queue depth alert (same spike as the 15:57 EDT alert)
• Queue was already draining to ~152 messages by alert time 16:02 EDT (baseline: 127)
• A *second spike began at ~16:05 EDT* (same pattern: ~1,267 → currently ~2,000 messages)
*Key pattern:* The two spikes this hour are exactly *3,600 seconds apart* — this is almost certainly an *hourly cron job* that bulk-publishes messages. First spike started ~15:18 EDT, second ~16:18 EDT. Queue drains in ~45 min each time.

*No backend errors, no Redis errors, no correlated deploys.*

*Likely cause:* Scheduled hourly batch job publishes a large message backlog (~2,700 msgs); workers drain it steadily. Today's behavior matches yesterday's baseline pattern (24h avg=1,024, max=2,672). The alert threshold may be too sensitive for this known workload.

*Suggested next action:* Confirm with the team whether this is the expected scheduled-job pattern. If yes, add a `false-alarm` KB entry to suppress these alerts (suggested: `silence_for: "2h"` with match on RabbitMQ queue + this cadence). If the queue fails to drain within the usual 45-min window, escalate.
